q: Of all the water on Earth, the percentage that is fresh water is _____
e: Of all the water on Earth, the percentage that is fresh water is 2.5%. 2.5% is the idea that completes this fact. 0.02% would fill a different blank than 2.5%.

q: The purest form of natural water is _____
e: The purest form of natural water is rain water. Rain water is the idea that completes this fact. Sea water would fill a different blank than rain water.

q: Sea water contains approximately _____ soluble salts.
e: Sea water contains approximately 3.5% soluble salts. 3.5% is the idea that completes this fact. 2.5% would fill a different blank than 3.5%.

q: Water reaches its maximum density at approximately _____
e: Water reaches its maximum density at approximately 4°C. 4°C is the idea that completes this fact. 100°C would fill a different blank than 4°C.

q: Water is regarded as the most universal solvent because it dissolves _____
a: almost all substances to some extent
e: Water is regarded as the most universal solvent because it dissolves almost all substances to some extent. Almost all substances to some extent is the idea that completes this fact. Only ionic compounds would fill a different blank than almost all substances to some extent.

q: Temporary hardness of water is caused by dissolved _____
e: Temporary hardness of water is caused by dissolved calcium hydrogen carbonate. Hydrogen is the lightest element and a common fuel and reducing agent in the lab. Calcium sulphate would fill a different blank than calcium hydrogen carbonate.

q: Permanent hardness is caused by dissolved calcium or magnesium _____
e: Permanent hardness is caused by dissolved calcium or magnesium chlorides and sulphates. Chlorides and sulphates is the idea that completes this fact. Nitrates would fill a different blank than chlorides and sulphates.

q: When soap is added to hard water, it forms an insoluble white precipitate known as _____
e: When soap is added to hard water, it forms an insoluble white precipitate known as scum. Scum is the idea that completes this fact. Sludge would fill a different blank than scum.

q: The degree of hardness of water is expressed in terms of parts per million of _____ equivalent.
e: The degree of hardness of water is expressed in terms of parts per million of CaCO₃ equivalent. CaCO₃ is the idea that completes this fact. MgCl₂ would fill a different blank than CaCO₃.

q: Water with a hardness of 150 ppm is classified as _____
e: Water with a hardness of 150 ppm is classified as hard. Hard water has a lot of calcium and magnesium ions, so soap does not lather well. Moderately hard would fill a different blank than hard.

q: Boiling removes _____ hardness from water.
e: Boiling removes temporary hardness from water. Temporary is the idea that completes this fact. Both types of would fill a different blank than temporary.

q: Washing soda softens hard water by precipitating calcium ions as _____
e: Washing soda softens hard water by precipitating calcium ions as calcium carbonate. Calcium carbonate is the idea that completes this fact. Calcium sulphate would fill a different blank than calcium carbonate.

q: In the Permutit method, sodium ions in zeolite are replaced by _____ from hard water.
e: In the Permutit method, sodium ions in zeolite are replaced by Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions from hard water. Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions is the idea that completes this fact. H⁺ ions would fill a different blank than Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions.

q: A common source of water pollution that introduces heavy metals like Pb and Hg is _____
e: A common source of water pollution that introduces heavy metals like Pb and Hg is industrial waste. Industrial waste is the idea that completes this fact. Agricultural runoff would fill a different blank than industrial waste.

q: Chlorination in water treatment is primarily used to _____
e: Chlorination in water treatment is primarily used to kill microorganisms. Kill microorganisms is the idea that completes this fact. Remove suspended particles would fill a different blank than kill microorganisms.

q: Distillation produces pure water but is not used on a large scale because it is _____
e: Distillation produces pure water but is not used on a large scale because it is far too expensive. Far too expensive is the idea that completes this fact. Ineffective is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: Fluorination of water is done to _____
e: Fluorination of water is done to prevent tooth decay. Prevent tooth decay is the idea that completes this fact. Improve taste would fill a different blank than prevent tooth decay.

q: Detergents do not form scum in hard water because their calcium and magnesium salts are _____
e: Detergents do not form scum in hard water because their calcium and magnesium salts are soluble. Soluble is the idea that completes this fact. Insoluble is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: Limescale in kettles is mainly composed of _____
e: Limescale in kettles is mainly composed of CaCO₃. CaCO₃ is the idea that completes this fact. CaSO₄ would fill a different blank than CaCO₃.

q: The chemical equation $\text{Ca(HCO}_3)_2(aq) \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{CaCO}_3(s) + \text{H}_2\text{O}(l) + \text{CO}_2(g)$ represents the removal of _____ hardness.
e: The chemical equation Ca(HCO3)2(aq) CaCO3(s) + H2O(l) + CO2(g) represents the removal of temporary hardness. Temporary is the idea that completes this fact. Permanent would fill a different blank than temporary.
